report.source_text: A 24-year-old woman presented to our dermatology clinic with a left posterior auricular papule and left preauricular papule present for 8 and 4 months, respectively (Figure 1). The patient had no significant medical or social history, including no tobacco or heavy alcohol use. Both lesions were painful and progressively enlarging. The patient denied any other symptoms.

report.source_text: The histology of both lesions demonstrated cellular dermal proliferations of epithelioid cells with the eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in cords within a myxohyaline stroma (Figure 2). Subtle vacuoles containing red blood cells were present within some of the cells (Figure 3). Histological and immunohistochemical findings were consistent with the diagnosis of EHE (Table 1).

report.source_text: Due to multifocal cutaneous disease, there was high clinical suspicion of metastatic disease. Our patient was referred to medical and surgical oncology for further evaluation, and computed tomography (CT) scans of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis were performed. Innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 1.8-cm hypoattenuated hepatic lesion, and prominent bilateral axillary lymph nodes were noted, all consistent with metastatic disease.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old woman presented with painful, progressively enlarging papules behind and in front of the left ear lasting 8 and 4 months. Biopsy of the lesions showed dermal proliferation of epithelioid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in cords within a myxohyaline stroma, with intracytoplasmic red blood cell-containing vacuoles. These histological features along with immunohistochemical findings (though not detailed) supported the diagnosis of EHE. Due to multifocal cutaneous disease, metastatic workup with CT scans revealed pulmonary nodules, a hepatic lesion, and axillary lymphadenopathy consistent with metastatic disease. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient elected watchful waiting with serial 3-month CT scans for monitoring.
